Author: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
Bench: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 31071 of 2023
Applicant :- Ashik

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohammad Waseem
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manoj Kumar Srivastava,Sandeep Kumar Rai
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.
Learned counsel for the informant is also present.

2. The applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 180 of 2023, under Sections 452, 376, 504,120-B IPC,
P.S. Bhojipura, District Bareilly during pendency of trial.

3. As per the prosecution case, a complaint was submitted by the victim at Police Station Bhojipura,
District Bareilly on 15.03.2023 to the effect that on 13.03.2023, all the members of the victim's family had went to sprinkle medicine in the mango orchard and the victim was alone at home.

It is alleged that at around 12.00 pm, victim's relatives, namely, Asif Khan, Daftar Khan and Avrar alias Mullu entered the victim's house and asked about victim's husband upon which victim said that her Ashik vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199949272/
1 husband is not at home and asked them to wait outside and thereafter she went inside of her house.
It is alleged that thereafter Asif Khan entered the room behind her and caught hold of victim and used force upon her and co accused Daftar Khan and Afsar Khan locked the room from outside.

It is further alleged that victim tried hard to free herself but Asif did not release Victim and raped her forcefully and thereafter Asif got opened the latch and went away from the spot threatening that if any action is taken then they would come again and now all the three would rape her.
4. It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that the applicant is not named in the FIR and even his implication has not surfaced anywhere during investigation.
It is further submitted that the FIR has been lodged after a gap of two and half days without there being any plausible explanation.

It is further submitted that the investigation has concluded and charge sheet has been filed against the accused Asif Khan son of Tehsil Khan whereas the two other named accused persons, namely Daftar Khan and Abrar @ Mullu have been exonerated from the present case.
It is further submitted that applicant has not committed any offence even then he has been booked in the present case as he is brother of the main accused Asif.

It is further submitted that in fact the marriage of victim's sister-in-law namely, Farhana has been solemnized with co accused Asif, who is real brother of the applicant and after some days of marriage, dispute arose between the co-accused Asif and his wife as a result of which a case under Section 498-A, 323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.
P. ACt has been registered against his whole family members and relatives.

It is further submitted that the victim being sister-in-law of the applicant's sister-in-law (Farhana), lodged the present false case against the applicant's brother and other family members in order to create pressure upon the applicant's family.
5. It is further stated that the victim in her statement said to have been recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that accused Asif Khan has raped her.
Applicant is brother of the applicant and has no concerned with the alleged crime and the allegation is against his brother Asif Khan.
The applicant is in jail since 26.05.2023 and has no previous criminal history.
Charge-sheet has been filed and conclusion of trial will take time, hence it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
6. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.

It is submitted that the applicant's whose name is Ashik is the main accused on the strength of the application for restitution of conjugal rights filed by this applicant wherein the name of the applicant is mentioned as Ashik and he has also placed reliance on the statements of the mother and brother of the applicant.

7. Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment as well as totality of facts and circumstances, at this stage without commenting on the merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
However, any observation made herein-above, will not affect the trial of the case.

8. Let the applicant- Ashik, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be Ashik vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199949272/
2 verified.
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A IPC.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial within a period of one year after the release of the applicant.
9.
In case of breach of of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

10. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
